_meta.source: Hud 04: German v2 (Nu->Noah, Elias->Ilyas x2; 'blieb ruhig und mutig' -> 'gab nicht auf', H55). No verse quoted in ﴿﴾; all in Oma's words (Hud 11:50-58, Fussilat 41:15, ash-Shu'ara 26:128-134, al-Fajr 89:7-8, al-Ahqaf 46:24-25, al-Haqqa 69:6-7).

s01: Shhh… Noah, Ilyas… what is stronger than the strongest people in the world? Stronger than huge castles and tall towers? Well, do you know? Tonight I will tell you. Come, snuggle in.
s02: Tonight it is about the Prophet Hud, peace be upon him.
s03: After Noah there lived a people called ʿAd. Allah had given them very special gifts. They were tall and incredibly strong.
s04: They built a city with huge pillars, called Iram. There was no city like it anywhere.
s05: Allah gave them gardens and springs, many animals and many children. But instead of thanking Allah, they became arrogant.
s06: On every hill they built tall towers just to show off. They built mighty castles as if they would live forever. And they were harsh and cruel to others.
s07: They even said: Who is stronger than us?
s08: Grandma, were they really that strong?
s09: Yes, Ilyas, but they had forgotten something: Allah, who created them, is much stronger than them.
s10: So Allah sent them a man from their own people: the Prophet Hud.
s11: He said: O my people, worship Allah alone; you have no god other than Him. If you ask Allah for forgiveness, He will send you plenty of rain and make you stronger.
s12: But they answered: You have brought us no proof, and we will not leave our gods. Perhaps one of our gods has struck you with something bad.
s13: But Hud did not give up. He said: I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord. Every living creature is in Allah’s hand.
s14: What do you think happened then?
s15: One day the people saw a huge dark cloud coming towards their valleys. They were happy and said: This is a cloud bringing us rain.
s16: But it was not rain. It was an icy, roaring wind. It blew for seven nights and eight days without stopping.
s17: And when the wind was over, nothing could be seen but their empty houses. But Allah saved the Prophet Hud and those who believed with him, by His mercy.
s18: The strongest castles and the tallest towers could not protect the people of ʿAd. Only Allah protects.
s19: Noah? Ilyas? They are already asleep.
s20: Sleep well, my little stars, and remember: true strength comes from Allah. When Allah gives us something, we say thank you and we do not become proud.
s21: And tomorrow I will tell you about the Prophet Salih and a wondrous camel. Good night.
